title: VPC installation prober and quota checklist for Private installs
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Context: Private (VPC) installs are failing late in the bootstrap flow when customers hit quota/permission/DNS issues that our install docs did not catch early. Current preinstall stories cover some checks but are fragmented (Terraform plan errors, IAM linting, manual docs). This ticket consolidates a reproducible, deterministic 'installation prober' that runs before any destructive operations and provides an actionable report (exit code + JSON) for CI, CLI, and onboarding engineers.

Goals:
- Implement a non-destructive install prober (redwoodctl install-probe) that validates: provider quotas (cores, GPUs, ENIs), IAM roles and required policies (cross-account roles, service-linked), DNS resolution for private zones and split-horizon setups, network prerequisites (subnets, route tables), key material and KMS permission checks, and minimal synthetic GPU allocation reservation as a smoke test where supported.
- Wire the prober into Terraform/IaC module outputs so that module authors can opt into the check during 'apply' (dry-run friendly).
- Produce a machine-readable report and human-friendly remediation hints. Report should include detection of soft-limit vs hard-limit, links to provider console pages where quota requests can be submitted, and an automated suggestion (e.g., required IAM policy snippet).
- Integrate into our Private install CI pipeline and the VPC onboarding runbook used by Solutions Engineering.

Design notes / constraints:
- Prober must be idempotent and run with least privileges; avoid creating long-lived resources. For GPU validation we will use ephemeral reservation APIs where available (e.g., AWS EC2 RunInstances with count 0 or capacity-verify API) or call DescribeInstanceTypeOfferings and DescribeInstanceTypes to validate quota-aware capacity instead of provisioning.
- For DNS we must validate both forward resolution and reverse resolution for internal hostnames, and detect split-horizon mismatches (private zone present in region A but not region B). Also verify that our TLS provisioner can reach the DNS provider API when certificates are requested.
- Terraform module integration: add a boolean flag module.install_probe_enable and an output module.install_probe_report_url. The probe should be runnable locally (redwoodctl) and in CI (helm job / GitHub Actions).
- Accessibility: produce both human summary and JSON schema v1.0 for automation. CLI should exit 0 on pass, 2 for warnings, 3 for fatal failures.

Acceptance criteria:
- redwoodctl install-probe implemented and documented in the Private install guide (Confluence link).
- Probe validates: core/GPU quotas, ENI & IP address availability, IAM role assumption and policy checks, DNS private zone resolution and certificate provisioning connectivity, KMS key usage checks, and basic observability (ability to reach Redwood control plane endpoints from VPC).
- CI integration: a gating job added to private-deploy repo that runs on PRs that touch Terraform modules; failures must provide remediation text with links.
- Unit and integration tests: create synthetic fixtures for AWS/Azure/GCP where applicable; add a nightly smoke job that runs probe against a minimal test VPC and uploads report to an internal dashboard.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement full automated quota increases (we will only detect and provide links/hints).
- It does not replace full end-to-end install tests; it aims to fail fast and provide deterministic guidance.

Related artifacts: Confluence design draft, Terraform module PR, initial prototype implementation in tools/install-prober (Python), dashboard prototype for reports.
acceptance_criteria: 1) redwoodctl install-probe exists and runs locally with clear human output plus --format=json machine output. 2) Detect and categorize quota issues (soft-limit, hard-limit, region-mismatch) for CPU, GPU, ENI, IPs. 3) Validate IAM: role exists, role can be assumed, required inline/managed policies present (list provided). 4) DNS: forward and reverse resolution succeed for private zone entries; detect split-horizon and provider API reachability for certs. 5) GPU check: capacity verified via descriptor calls (no destructive provisioning) or ephemeral reservation where supported. 6) CI job added and green on a minimal test VPC; failures documented with remediation links.

2026-02-15 - Samir Gupta: Spike complete. Prototype exists in tools/install-prober/README.md. Prototype uses DescribeInstanceTypes + DescribeAccountAttributes to validate quotas on AWS; needs Azure/GCP adapters. Pushed spike branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/198

2026-02-25 - Design (Maya Alvarez): UX for CLI: show 'Remediation card' per failure with a one-click copy policy snippet and a 'Request quota increase' URL. We should upstream snippet templates to terraform-modules repo.

2026-02-27 - Samir Gupta: Implemented JSON schema v1.0 and CLI exit codes; PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/412. Blocker: we need a service account with Describe quotas permission for Azure subscription used by nightly tests. Filed dependency ENG-74290.

notes: Implementation approach: build adapters for AWS/Azure/GCP quota APIs, reuse terraform state outputs where available, and add a small terraform helper module that emits 'probe metadata' to be consumed by redwoodctl. For GPU types, maintain a curated list of instance families per cloud and prefer descriptor APIs over provisioning. Add e2e nightly test that runs probe against ephemeral test VPC in staging. Communicate changes in the oncall runbook and support playbook.
